slides.caption: Nothing runs until you call output(), status() or spawn().
The program and its arguments are set up.
output() runs it and collects what it printed.
The program is found through PATH, like in a terminal.

arg.title: How Command::arg works
arg.description: Adds one argument to the command.

slides.caption: Each argument is passed as-is: no shell, so spaces and quotes need no escaping.

output.title: How Command::output works
output.description: Runs the program, waits for it, and collects its output.

slides.caption: stdout and stderr come back as Vec<u8>.
The program runs to the end.
String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout) turns the bytes into text.

status.title: How Command::status works
status.description: Runs the program and returns only its exit status.

slides.caption: The child prints directly to your terminal; you only get the exit code.
st.code() gives the number (None if killed by a signal).
Each item is one argument, passed as-is.
arg() adds one at a time.
Handy for logging what will be run.

get_program.title: How Command::get_program works
get_program.description: The program the command will run.

slides.caption: Returns exactly what was passed to new().

env.title: How Command::env works
env.description: Sets an environment variable for the child process only.

slides.caption: The parent's environment is not touched.

envs.title: How Command::envs works
envs.description: Sets several environment variables for the child.

slides.caption: Any iterator of (key, value) pairs works.
Pass a HashMap of settings directly.

env_remove.title: How Command::env_remove works
env_remove.description: Removes a variable from the child's environment.

slides.caption: The child will not see it.

env_clear.title: How Command::env_clear works
env_clear.description: Starts the child with an empty environment.

slides.caption: Useful for reproducible or sandboxed runs.
Some programs need PATH; add it back if so.

get_envs.title: How Command::get_envs works
get_envs.description: The environment changes recorded for the child.

slides.caption: Only changes are listed, not the inherited variables.

current_dir.title: How Command::current_dir works
current_dir.description: Sets the working directory for the child.

slides.caption: Relative paths in the child resolve against this folder.

get_current_dir.title: How Command::get_current_dir works
get_current_dir.description: The working directory set for the child, if any.

slides.caption: None means the child uses the parent's directory.

spawn.title: How Command::spawn works
spawn.description: Starts the child and returns immediately with a Child handle.

slides.caption: Unlike output() and status(), spawn does not wait.
Remember to wait, or the child may become a zombie on Unix.

stdout.title: How Command::stdout works
stdout.description: Chooses where the child's standard output goes.

slides.caption: piped() lets you read it; null() discards it; inherit() shows it.

stderr.title: How Command::stderr works
stderr.description: Chooses where the child's error output goes.

slides.caption: Error messages go to stderr, not stdout.

note.text: result: has error text: true, success: false

stdin.title: How Command::stdin works
stdin.description: Chooses where the child reads its standard input from.

slides.caption: piped() lets you write to it; null() gives immediate end-of-file.
The child sees EOF at once.
Avoids children hanging while waiting for input.

piped.title: How Stdio::piped works
piped.description: Connects a child stream to a pipe the parent can use.

slides.caption: The parent holds the other end.
Read it before wait(), or a full pipe can block the child.

null.title: How Stdio::null works
null.description: Connects a child stream to nothing (discard output, empty input).

slides.caption: For stdin it means immediate end-of-file.

inherit.title: How Stdio::inherit works
inherit.description: The child shares the parent's stream (e.g. prints to your terminal).

slides.caption: No pipe; the output goes where yours goes.
Nothing to read in the parent.

wait.title: How Child::wait works
wait.description: Waits for the child to exit and returns its status.

slides.caption: Closes the child's stdin first, so it is not left waiting for input.
The child runs to the end.

wait_with_output.title: How Child::wait_with_output works
wait_with_output.description: Waits for the child and collects its piped output.

slides.caption: Reads the pipes while waiting, so a full pipe cannot block.

try_wait.title: How Child::try_wait works
try_wait.description: Checks if the child has exited, without blocking.

slides.caption: Poll a child while doing other work.
Loop with a short sleep, or use wait.

kill.title: How Child::kill works
kill.description: Forces the child process to stop.

slides.caption: Then wait() collects the exit status.
wait() reports it did not succeed.

id.title: How Child::id works
id.description: The operating-system process ID of the child.

slides.caption: Useful for logging or OS tools.
IDs are reused after the process exits.

success.title: How ExitStatus::success works
success.description: true if the process exited with code 0.

slides.caption: Programs signal failure with a non-zero exit code.

code.title: How ExitStatus::code works
code.description: The numeric exit code, if the process exited normally.

note.text: None if killed by a signal

slides.caption: 0 is success; other numbers are program-specific errors.

process-id.title: How process::id works
process-id.description: The process ID of the current program.

slides.caption: Handy for log lines and lock files.

exit.title: How process::exit works
exit.description: Ends the program right away with an exit code.

slides.caption: Destructors of the current stack do not run; stdout is flushed.
Returning from main is usually cleaner.

abort.title: How process::abort works
abort.description: Stops the program abnormally, at once.

slides.caption: No destructors, no unwinding, no flushing.
panic! unwinds first; abort does not.
